exercise.name: 3 Leg Dog Pose

reference.title: 3 Leg Dog Pose (female)
reference.note: Used only to identify the movement. This rig, artwork and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (closed chain through hands and feet)
exercise.laterality: Bilateral dog, then unilateral leg lift (alternate sides)

muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Main stretch of the standing leg: hips high, knee nearly straight.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Stretched as the standing heel reaches toward the floor (ankle dorsiflexed about 30 degrees).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extends the hip to lift the right leg up and back.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Help the glute hold the lifted leg in line with the trunk.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the arm overhead under body weight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the arm overhead under body weight.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Keeps the elbow long without locking it.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Keeps the elbow long without locking it.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the standing knee straight so the hamstrings can lengthen.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Pushes the floor away so the shoulder blade wraps the rib cage.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Pushes the floor away so the shoulder blade wraps the rib cage.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the pelvis level and stops the low back arching when the leg lifts.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the spine long instead of rounded.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the spine long instead of rounded.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Stops the hips sagging or shifting toward the standing leg.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the hips lift up and back into down dog; inhale as the right leg lifts up and back; breathe slowly and evenly in the hold; exhale as the leg lowers; inhale as you shift forward to plank.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s into dog, 1.8 s lift, 2.2 s hold (1 to 2 breaths in a real set), 1.6 s lower, 2 s back to plank

prescription.flow: 4 to 6 lift-and-lower reps per side, 1 to 2 breaths at the top
prescription.staticOption: 3 to 5 breaths (about 15 to 25 s) in three-legged dog per side
prescription.dogHold: 10 to 15 s or several breaths between sides
prescription.tempo: 2-2-2-2-2 (into dog, lift, hold, lower, back to plank)

cues.text: High plank: hands shoulder-width, fingers spread, press through the index finger and thumb. Body in one line.
Breathe out and lift the hips up and back into an upside-down V. Lift from the hips and roll over the toes; the hands stay put.
Push the floor away, head relaxed between the upper arms. Keep the back long; bend the knees a little if it rounds. Heels reach toward the floor but do not need to touch.
Breathe in and lift the right leg up and back, in line with the trunk. Hips stay level and square to the floor; toes point down.
Breathe slowly. Weight stays even in both hands; reach back through the lifted heel.
Breathe out and lower the right foot back beside the left.
Breathe in and shift forward through dog to plank. Repeat, then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Rounded back, usually from tight hamstrings or shoulders
mistakes.fix: Bend the knees and send the hips up and back until the spine is long.

mistakes.mistake: Opening the hip or cranking the leg too high
mistakes.fix: Lower the leg until both hip points face the floor again; aim for the leg in line with the trunk.

mistakes.mistake: Hands and feet too close together or too far apart
mistakes.fix: Adjust the distance until the spine can lengthen; feet about hip-width.

mistakes.mistake: Weight sinking into the heel of the hand or the outer wrist
mistakes.fix: Press the index finger and thumb down so the palm arches.

mistakes.mistake: Shoulders collapsing or elbows locking back
mistakes.fix: Push the floor away and keep a micro-bend in the elbows.

mistakes.mistake: Forcing the heels to the floor
mistakes.fix: Let the heels lift, or support them on a rolled towel or mat.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the head or tensing the neck
mistakes.fix: Let the head hang between the arms with the neck long.

kinematics.norm: About 83° in a wall-supported dog; 49° and 67° means (ranges up to about 92 to 95°) in Parvatasana; rig target 80 to 90°
About 160 to 175°, head between the upper arms (estimate); AAOS reference maximum 180°
Peak 30.5° (SD 11.4°) in Parvatasana; about 13° in a wall-supported dog; AAOS 20° non-weight-bearing
No measured value; leg in line with the trunk (hip near 0°), at most 10 to 20° past with the pelvis level (AAOS hip extension 20°)

kinematics.peak: Level: both hip points face the floor, no hip opening
kinematics.norm: Square-hip version (the open-hip variant is a separate pose)

cautions: Wrist, shoulder or ankle injury: Yoga Journal advises avoiding the pose; try a modified version instead.
High blood pressure, glaucoma, heart problems, dizziness or fainting: check with a clinician first, as the head is below the heart.
Stop if you feel pain; warm up first and work within your limits.
modify: Sore wrists: a rolled towel under the heels of the hands, one forearm down, or hands on a wall or desk.
Tight hamstrings, calves or low back pain: bend the knees, or press the heels against a wall.
Balance or shoulder fatigue: keep both feet down, or lift the leg only a few centimetres.
regressions: Bent-knee down dog without the leg lift.
Hands on a wall or desk (standing dog).
progressions: Hold three-legged dog for 5 or more breaths per side.
Slow lift-and-lower reps with a 1 to 2 breath pause at the top.
